Bodzentyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bodzentyn, Poland

Not demolished. Until an independent Jewish community was established, Bodzentyn's Jews were under the supervision of, and buried by, the synagogue in Szydłowiec; they received permission to establish this cemetery in 1866. After the 1942 liquidation of the Bodzentyn Ghetto — whose roughly 3,700 residents included Dawid Rubinowicz, author of a well-known ghetto diary, later deported to Treblinka via Suchedniów — the Germans partially destroyed the cemetery, and locals further damaged it after the war. The mother of the writer Gustaw Herling-Grudziński is buried here. In 2006, local priest Leszek Sikorski and culture animator Krystyna Nowakowska initiated a cleanup, joined by local Jewish descendant Max (Manes) Safir, who helped raise restoration funds with the Swedish Committee against Antisemitism; the restored cemetery reopened on August 26, 2009.
